summary: מָה asks what something is, and with לְ it asks why. It can also express wonder, as when Psalm 8 celebrates the majesty of Yahweh’s name.

senses.definition: Ask for the identity, nature or significance of something. Moses asks what he should say when asked for God’s name. Psalm 8 asks what a mortal is that God remembers him.
With the preposition לְ, the question asks for a reason. The psalm asks why the nations gather against Yahweh and why Yahweh seems to stand far off.
The question word can introduce an exclamation of wonder or distress. Psalm 8 opens and closes by marveling at the majesty of Yahweh’s name.
In an embedded question it introduces the thing to be discovered. Mordecai walks before the court to learn how Esther fares and what will happen to her.
The question asks what someone is doing. In a report the word introduces what will happen or what is needed.
With a prefixed preposition the word asks the reason for the urgency of a decree or for letting harm come to a king.
With the comparison prefix it introduces a cry of admiration at God’s signs and wonders.
The Peshitta uses the pronoun in expressions introducing an occasion, such as giving to the poor, praying or fasting.

evidence.locator: s.v. מָה II, Jerusalem Talmud Gittin I, 43d
evidence.note: The question asks what case is under discussion.

note: The Hebrew interrogative is a rootless key in the corpus index. Many Aramaic-key surface matches occur in Hebrew contexts. SEDRA lexeme 1696 is the short Syriac form, while the longer interrogative מָנָא is filed under מנ.
